name: Assisted Pull-up
machineIdentification: A tall frame with pull-up handles at the top and a padded platform for your knees hanging below. The weight stack is behind the platform — more weight means more help, not less.
instructions: Set the assistance weight, then step onto the side rails.
Grip the handles slightly wider than your shoulders.
Kneel carefully onto the padded platform and let it settle.
Pull yourself up until your chin clears the handles.
Lower under control until your arms are straight.
keyCues: Drive your elbows down toward your ribs, not back.
Start each rep from a full hang.
Take three seconds to lower yourself.
commonMistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom instead of pulling from a dead hang.
Using so much assistance that the top half does all the work.
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears at the start.

name: Lat Pulldown
machineIdentification: A seat with a thigh pad above it and a long straight bar hanging from a high pulley. The thigh pad is what stops you lifting off the seat.
instructions: Set the thigh pad so it holds your legs down firmly.
Grip the bar wider than shoulder width, palms facing away.
Sit down and let your arms straighten fully.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, leaning back slightly.
Let the bar rise back up under control.
keyCues: Pull with your elbows, not your hands.
Keep your chest lifted toward the bar.
Stop the bar at your collarbone, not behind your neck.
commonMistakes: Leaning far back and turning it into a row.
Letting the weight yank your shoulders up at the top.
Pulling the bar behind the neck, which stresses the shoulders.

name: Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown
machineIdentification: Same station as the lat pulldown, but clip on the V-shaped handle or the bar with parallel grips at the ends, so your palms face each other.
instructions: Attach the V-handle or parallel-grip bar to the high pulley.
Set the thigh pad snug against your legs.
Sit and take the handle with palms facing each other.
Pull the handle to your upper chest.
Return to a full stretch under control.
keyCues: Keep your wrists straight and neutral.
Lead with the elbows, finish with the chest.
Pause briefly at the bottom of each rep.
commonMistakes: Rocking the torso to generate momentum.
Cutting the range short at the top.
Gripping so hard the forearms fail before the back does.

name: Pull-up
machineIdentification: A fixed horizontal bar above head height — on a power rack, a wall-mounted frame, or the top of a cable tower.
instructions: Grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders, palms away.
Hang with arms straight and shoulders engaged.
Pull until your chin clears the bar.
Lower all the way down under control.
keyCues: Squeeze your glutes to stop the legs swinging.
Pull your chest toward the bar.
Own the lowering half — that's where the growth is.
commonMistakes: Kipping or swinging to get through the sticking point.
Stopping halfway down and losing the stretch.
Letting the shoulders creep up into a shrug at the bottom.

name: Seated Cable Row
machineIdentification: A long bench or seat at floor level with a foot plate in front and a low pulley between your feet. Usually a V-handle is already clipped on.
instructions: Sit with feet braced on the plate, knees slightly bent.
Take the handle and sit tall with arms extended.
Pull the handle to your belly button.
Hold for a beat with shoulder blades squeezed.
Let your arms straighten fully before the next rep.
keyCues: Keep your torso still — the arms move, not the back.
Pull the handle low, to the navel not the chest.
Let the shoulder blades spread apart at the front.
commonMistakes: Rowing with the lower back by rocking forward and back.
Rounding the spine at the front of the movement.
Shrugging the shoulders instead of retracting them.

name: Chest-Supported Row Machine
machineIdentification: A seat facing a large angled chest pad, with handles either side at chest height. Your chest rests against the pad so your lower back does nothing.
instructions: Set the seat height so the handles line up with your mid-chest.
Sit with your chest firmly against the pad.
Take the handles with arms extended.
Pull the handles back until your elbows pass your ribs.
Return slowly to a full stretch.
keyCues: Keep your chest glued to the pad the whole set.
Drive the elbows back and slightly down.
Pause for a second at the squeeze.
commonMistakes: Peeling the chest off the pad to move more weight.
Jerking the handles and letting them snap back.
Setting the seat too low, which turns it into a shrug.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
machineIdentification: Any flat bench plus a single dumbbell. You brace one hand and one knee on the bench and row with the other arm.
instructions: Place your left hand and left knee on a flat bench.
Set your right foot on the floor, back roughly parallel to the ground.
Hold the dumbbell in your right hand, arm hanging straight.
Row the dumbbell to the side of your ribs.
Lower it all the way down, then repeat and switch sides.
keyCues: Keep your back flat like a tabletop.
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, not your shoulder.
Don't let your torso rotate as you pull.
commonMistakes: Twisting the shoulders open to finish the rep.
Rounding the lower back under heavier dumbbells.
Yanking with the arm instead of driving the elbow back.

name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
machineIdentification: A standard barbell, loaded on the floor or in a rack at knee height. No dedicated machine.
instructions: Stand with feet hip width, barbell over your mid-foot.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is 45 degrees or lower.
Grip the bar just outside your knees.
Row the bar to your lower ribs.
Lower it under control without standing up.
keyCues: Lock your torso angle and hold it all set.
Brace your core hard before the first rep.
Pull the bar into your body, not up toward your chest.
commonMistakes: Standing up a little on every rep to help the weight.
Rounding the lower back under load.
Choosing a weight that turns it into a partial-range jerk.

name: Inverted Row
machineIdentification: A bar fixed at roughly hip height — a Smith machine bar or a rack's safety bar both work. You hang underneath it with your heels on the floor.
instructions: Set a bar at about hip height.
Lie underneath and grip it slightly wider than your shoulders.
Hang with heels on the floor and body in a straight line.
Pull your chest to the bar.
Lower until your arms are straight.
keyCues: Squeeze your glutes so your hips don't sag.
Touch your chest to the bar on every rep.
Raise the bar to make it easier, lower it to make it harder.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips drop so it becomes an arm pull.
Only going halfway up.
Craning the neck to reach the bar first.

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
machineIdentification: A cable tower with the pulley set high and a straight bar or rope attached. You stand facing it, a step back from the frame.
instructions: Set the pulley high and attach a straight bar.
Stand a step back, feet hip width, slight hinge at the hips.
Hold the bar with arms straight, roughly at eye level.
Sweep the bar down to your thighs, keeping arms straight.
Let it rise back up under control.
keyCues: Keep a soft, fixed bend in the elbows the whole time.
Feel the stretch under your armpits at the top.
Move only at the shoulder joint.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows and turning it into a pushdown.
Using so much weight the torso rocks to help.
Standing too close, which kills the range of motion.
